Final categorization: OK  
(Justification: The paper presents original research focused on national-scale LULC prediction in Japan. It explicitly develops and validates land-use scenarios at the national level using a 500 m spatial resolution dataset covering the entire country (472,580 km²). The primary objective is to assess and improve LULC simulation accuracy by comparing multiple scenarios—including Business-as-Usual and four PANCES scenarios—though the validation focuses on BaU, the modeling framework supports ≥2 future scenarios with quantitative narrative and policy-based differentiation. The study implements spatially explicit modeling via Land Change Modeler, produces mapped LULC projections for 1987–2014 and forward to 2050, and employs quantitative accuracy metrics including Figure of Merit (FOM), intensity analysis, and decomposition into hits, misses, and false alarms to evaluate both quantity and allocation disagreement. All core inclusion criteria are met: national-scale implementation, primary focus on LULC prediction, use of multiple future scenarios (even if validation uses one, the system simulates multiple), spatial modeling with quantitative validation, and mapped outputs. None of the exclusion criteria apply—it is not global/local, not species/ecology-focused, not purely economic, includes LULC change analysis, is applied (not methodological only), includes future projections beyond BAU alone, and uses spatially explicit predictive modeling.)
